material_gaps: No held instrument expressly revokes, terminates or supersedes EO 13159: EO 13617 (77 FR 38459) re-declares a new emergency and re-blocks the same HEU-related property but contains no revocation or supersession verb and in sec. 2 treats licenses issued under EO 13159 as continuing; the supersession is an inference, not a held express ending.
Continuation notices after June 17, 2010 (2011, 2012, later) are not held, so the life of the EO 13159 national emergency (IEEPA/NEA annual continuation) cannot be traced.
notice: Producer research decision only. Independent review and owner adoption remain separate.
rationale: BLOCKED, leaning NO. I read the complete held EO 13159 (65 FR 39279, June 21, 2000: declares a national emergency, blocks Russian Federation property directly related to the HEU Agreements; sec. 6(a) effective June 22, 2000; no sunset, no savings clause) and the complete held EO 13617 (77 FR 38459, June 25, 2012), which declares a fresh national emergency, repeats the sec. 2 blocking in near-identical words 'except to the extent provided in regulations, orders, directives, or licenses that may be issued pursuant to this order, or that were issued pursuant to Executive Order 13159' and adds anti-evasion/conspiracy provisions. 13617 is a replacement in function but nowhere says 13159 is revoked, superseded or terminated, and an IEEPA emergency continues by annual notice until terminated; the catalog 'See:' list shows continuation notices only through June 17, 2010. Treating the overlap as an ending would be inference beyond the held text. EO 12938 and 13085 (read only for the cross-references) are background policy orders, not endings. The history is only a catalog cross-reference list (dates in it are dates of the referenced instruments, not events). To settle: the 2011-2012 continuation/termination notices and the Treasury/OFAC rule or FR note that states the relationship of EO 13617 to EO 13159.
